physical.mounting-hardware: M6 cup screw and nut x12

front.description: Option 1 of the guide: the bracket on the front face of the post, its foot at the rear end of the plate.

rear.description: Option 2 of the guide, "Back Side": the bracket on the rear face of the post, its foot at the front end of the plate.

description: Vertical PDU mounting brackets, FS SKU #78523, two to a pack. Each is a short black SPCC steel bracket that bolts to a rack post and holds a zero-U PDU beside it. A foot 30 mm across lies against the post and is bolted through four holes. A plate 135 mm deep and 88.4 mm high stands out from it. Three gussets join it to the foot, and each long edge turns back into a short lip. The plate has three keyhole slots, which take the mounting buttons of a toolless PDU, and two rows of four square holes. The guide shows two ways to fit it, on the front of the post or on its rear side.

gaps.note: the data sheet FS links for this SKU is the FS-GR42U-PDUBK sheet, which is the cabinet bracket and no part of this one. The quick start guide carries no dimension and no weight.
gaps.wanted: a data sheet or a drawing of FS-PDUBK from FS

gaps.note: no document held states the bracket's weight.
FS states the material, SPCC, and no thickness for any part of the bracket.

the guide gives no keyhole size and the dimensioned render gives only the pitch. The width scaled off it, 11.5, meets what the connectors registry states for `pdu-button` and is not confirmed by a figure.

the lip and the gusset sizes are estimates read from the photographs. The bends at the foot and at the two lips are rounded, about 2 to 4 mm radius (x7, g2, g3), and are drawn square. The gussets and the lips are not drawn in 3D. `relief.features` with `shape: true` was tried on the gusset and the lip. The blocks stood outside the top and bottom faces, because the shape extrudes outward, so it was reverted.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side or top drawing of the bracket

gaps.note: each lip ends in a small hook past the plate's free end, one at each long edge (x6, g5, x7, g2, g3). Each hook reaches 3.2 to 3.5 mm past the plate end and stands 2.4 to 2.7 mm high. The reach is read on the two plan pictures, each at the scale of a dimension in it. On x6 it reads 20 to 21 px at 6.04 to 6.18 px per mm, from its printed 135 line and its printed 31.5 pitch. On g5 it reads 21 to 22 px at 6.52 to 6.56 px per mm, from the plate's 135 and the same pitch. The perspective pictures x7, g2 and g3 show the hooks but give no usable reach. A dark band about 1.2 mm wide runs down the end edge between them. In the built views the plate and its lips end flush at 135. The printed 135 line on x6 ends 1.5 mm short of the plate's end edge, so a reading from that line gives 140. The 135 is printed on x6, the product page's dimensioned drawing, as 5.3" (135mm). The quick start guide prints no dimension. The kit can hold the hooks if the four views and the chassis depth all read 139. A trial with the depth and the four views at 139 printed "HEAD level 4 addressable" then "working tree level 4 addressable". The device lint passed. The device lock asked for a major version beyond 1.0.0 for the depth and view change alone, and no id was lost. The built views were not tested. Widening only the four views to 138 dropped the bracket from level 4 to level 2. It printed "blocked 3 solid - chassis depth disagrees: left.w=138, right.w=138, top.h=138, bottom.h=138, chassis.depth=135". A test asserts "an inconsistent box must not reach solid". The depth stays at the printed 135 and the hooks are not drawn, because a stated dimension is the maintainer's to change.
gaps.wanted: the maintainer's yes that the stated depth may read 139 so the hooks can be drawn, or a drawing that dimensions the hooks

foot.description: the sheet that lies against the post, bolted through four holes

keyholes.description: the slots a PDU's mounting buttons seat in

plate.description: the sheet that stands out from the foot, with the keyholes and the square holes

name: fs-pdubk

chassis.note: drawing - 135 and 88.4 are the dimensions of the product page's render of the plate (5.3 in [135 mm] and 3.5 in [88.4 mm]). The product page's specification gives 30 x 135 x 88.4 mm (H x W x D as FS prints it); the 30 is the foot's reach from the plate and no view dimensions it. Each long edge of the plate turns back into a lip. The lips stand about 5 clear of the plate on the side away from the foot. So the part is 30 plus 5, 35, across the rack's face, 88.4 high and 135 deep. THE 5 AND THE 35 ARE ESTIMATED, and FS does not say whether its 30 counts the lip. It was settled from two perspective photographs of the product page. The plate's known 135 by 88.4 gave each camera, and heights above the plate followed from it. The foot reaches 30 from the plate's underside: 28 above its top face, and 29.5 to 31.1 in the two pictures. Foot plus lip comes to about 35, not 30. So the 30 is the foot's reach alone, and the lip is added to it.

color.note: black, as every photograph of the product page shows, and FS's "SPCC" for the steel. The photographs measure a neutral near-black, with no blue cast. Pixels of luminance under 90 average 60 (n=431,329, x6), 48 (n=361,667, x7), 47 (n=215,802, g1) and 60 (n=493,471, g5). The fills stay as the device uses them, body #1b1d20 and edges #2a2d31, because colours are a later touch.

fit.note: the guide's Option 1 figure fixes the PDU's own ears to the plate through the square holes with four screws; its Option 2 figure hangs the PDU by a button in a keyhole. Only the keyholes are modelled as slots a PDU's buttons are matched to. The square holes are drawn and not published.

foot.note: estimated - four bolt holes, two round between two slotted, up the foot's middle, drawn on the EIA-310 pattern (15.875, 12.7 and 15.875 up the post, 44.45 end to end) that the photographs' spacing agrees with, centred on the 88.4. Round 6.6 across, slotted 6.6 by 10.5. The slots run across the foot, at right angles to the column of holes, with a small tail at the end toward the plate. The foot's two free corners are rounded, radius about 4, and three gussets join it to the plate (fs/fs-pdubk-flange@1). The guide's Step 1 shows the foot bolted to the post's holes with cup screws and nuts.

gussets.note: estimated - three gussets join the plate to the foot. They stand at 12.7, 44.2 and 75.7 down the 88.4, the 31.5 pitch of the keyholes about the middle. Each is a right triangle about 15 across the foot and 6 along the plate. It is 6.5 thick at the plate and 3.5 at the tip. Both were counted in pixels on the dimensioned render at 6.65 px per mm (fs/fs-pdubk-gusset-plan@1 and the skins of the foot and the plate). The top view shows the top one, the bottom view the bottom one.

hardware.note: the guide's accessories figure shows 12 pieces, each an M6 cup screw with its nut, for the two brackets; the product listing says the same.

keyhole.note: estimated - the guide gives no slot size. The slot scaled off the render is 11.5 wide, which is the lower end of the 11.5 to 12.5 mm the Eaton Rack PDU G4 installation guide (P-164001156 rev 3, 2.11) asks of a keyhole in 1.5 to 2 mm sheet and the width the connectors registry states for `pdu-button`; it does not differ from the registry note. The button seats in the lower narrow end, 26.3 mm up the plate from its bottom: the guide's Option 2 figure draws the button at the bottom of the middle keyhole, and a PDU hangs by its weight. Every keyhole stands at that height, so each configuration publishes three slots at the same height.

lip.note: estimated - each long edge of the plate turns back into a lip, away from the side the foot is on. Each lip is about 5 mm clear of the plate and runs the plate's whole 135. The hook at the end of each lip reaches 3.2 to 3.5 mm past the plate's end (gap `lip-end-tabs`). The two perspective photographs give 4.6 to 5.1 below the plate's underside. In the front and the rear view each lip is a bar beside the plate's edge. One is at the top and one at the bottom of the 88.4. The top and the bottom view show the upper and the lower lip as a strip along the plate (fs/fs-pdubk-lip-plan@1). The view from the side away from the foot shows both as bars along the plate's top and bottom edges. The foot's side shows neither, as they lie behind the plate. The far short end of the plate is a plain edge in every photograph.

method.note: FS-PDUBK HAS NO DATA SHEET OF ITS OWN. FS's documentation link and its shop link for this SKU both serve the FS-GR42U-PDUBK data sheet, the full-height cabinet bracket (1974 x 135 x 10, M4 screws), which is a different part and is not used. The sources are the FS-PDUBK Quick Start Guide V1.0 (two pages, images only, no dimension on either), the gallery of the product page (SKU 78523), and the product page's one dimensioned drawing of the plate, a render. That drawing gives 135 and 88.4 and the 31.5 pitch of the keyholes and of the square holes; every other position here is scaled off it or off the photographs, on the axis it lies along, and says so.

mount.note: `rack-side`, which is the library's one way to say a part stands vertically beside the rack, on a post, and takes no rack unit of its own (docs/vertical-cable-managers-design.md): the guide's Step 1 bolts two of them to a post, one near the top and one near the bottom, and Step 2 hangs a vertical PDU on the pair. `ru: 2` is the 88.4 mm it runs, 1.99 units. It is drawn as it stands beside the rack: the front is its foot, 30 across, with the plate going away from it along the depth of the rack. THE ORIENTATION IS READ OFF THE PHOTOGRAPHS AND THE GUIDE'S FIGURES, NOT A DRAWING: the foot lies on a post's face, so it is a plane across the rack and the plate stands at right angles to it, along the depth, which is where a PDU hung on its keyholes stands. Which edge of the foot the plate is on, left or right, is not stated, and the plate is drawn on the right of the front view.

options.note: the guide's two ways to fit it are its two configurations. `front` is Option 1, the bracket on the front face of the post, so its foot is at the rear end of the plate and the plate runs forward of the post. `rear` is Option 2 ("Back Side"), the bracket on the post's rear face, so its foot is at the front end and the plate runs behind the post. ESTIMATED: the guide's figures show a PDU hung beside the bracket and the plate's face to the viewer and do not show which end of the plate the foot is at, so that is read from where the post is in each figure. The keyholes stand at the same height in both, and so do the squares, because it is the same part turned end for end.

plate.note: estimated - the plate scaled off the dimensioned render, each position on the axis it lies along: the render's own dimensions give 6.25 px/mm along the plate and 6.66 px/mm across it, 6 per cent apart, so it carries a little perspective and no position is taken across both axes at one scale. Three keyholes 31.5 apart (dimensioned) at 38.4, 69.9 and 101.4 from the foot's end of the plate (the first scaled), each a narrow slot 11.5 wide and 47.3 long with a wider opening 21.3 across and 19 high at its middle, centred up the 88.4; four columns of square holes about 9 across, 31.5 apart (dimensioned), at 22.9, 54.4, 85.9 and 117.4, in two rows centred 10.3 from the top and from the bottom.

thickness.note: estimated - `shell: sheet`, 2.0: FS states the material (SPCC) and not the gauge, and the sheet body builds no floor thinner than 2 mm (docs/cable-managers-design.md section 4). The solid in 3D is the plate and the foot, each a well; the six views are elevations.
